line: FORCED: D2 vs C2 -- MEANS [CR3]: "the text says Joseph did not know her until the birth -- [L2] ginōskō G1097 (to know) | [L3] Genesis 4:1 "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived"" -- ANSWER [DR3]: "Matthew orders the events: 1. The finding: "before they came together, she was found with child" (Matthew 1:18). 2. The taking: "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24). The law names that same step: "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her" (Deuteronomy 20:7). 3. The abstinence: "knew her not till." "Till" (heōs) sets the bound. The abstinence covers the pregnancy, from the taking to the birth. Genesis 4:1 gives the knowing that precedes conception. In Matthew's order, that knowing falls before the finding, within the espousal. It fits the link." -- FAILS: "In Matthew's order, that knowing falls before the finding, within the espousal."

The husband-and-wife state of 1:19-20 runs before that taking, and the knowing of the chain falls inside it. *synerchomai* (G4905) includes \"assemble... come together,\" which is the household convening of 1:24." -- FAILS: "*synerchomai* (G4905) includes \"assemble... come together,\" which is the household convening of 1:24."

FORCED: D1 vs C1 -- MEANS [CR3]: "the finding precedes any coming together, so no union lies behind it" -- ANSWER [DR3]: "The row dates the finding by the coming together. Synerchomai (G4905) means "to come together, assemble, cohabit." Matthew shows the coming together six verses later with the verb of 1:20's command, paralambanō (G3880, "to receive near... take unto"). Matthew 1:24 reads: "and took unto him his wife." The law calls the betrothed a wife before she is taken: "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband" (Deuteronomy 22:23), "his neighbour's wife" (22:24). So "before they came together" means before the taking of 1:24. The espousal, in which she is already his wife, precedes it. "Of the Holy Ghost" stands as the origin-marker answered under Link 2. This fits the link: the union lies within the espousal, and the finding lies before the taking." -- FAILS: "So "before they came together" means before the taking of 1:24."
